problem_text:
A regional airline must design a flight circuit connecting seven airports, each with distinct geographical coordinates:

Airport Alpha: Position (53,96)
Airport Bravo: Position (150,74)
Airport Charlie: Position (2,35)
Airport Delta: Position (38,69)
Airport Echo: Position (85,86)
Airport Foxtrot: Position (94,183)
Airport Golf: Position (23,86)

The flight distances in nautical miles between these airports are predetermined:
Alpha to Charlie: 79.5 nm
Alpha to Delta: 30.9 nm
Alpha to Echo: 33.5 nm
Alpha to Foxtrot: 96.2 nm
Alpha to Golf: 31.6 nm
Bravo to Charlie: 153.1 nm
Bravo to Delta: 112.1 nm
Bravo to Echo: 66.1 nm
Bravo to Foxtrot: 122.5 nm
Bravo to Golf: 127.6 nm
Charlie to Delta: 49.5 nm
Charlie to Echo: 97.4 nm
Charlie to Foxtrot: 174.3 nm
Charlie to Golf: 55.2 nm
Delta to Echo: 50.0 nm
Delta to Foxtrot: 127.0 nm
Delta to Golf: 22.7 nm
Echo to Foxtrot: 97.4 nm
Echo to Golf: 62.0 nm
Foxtrot to Golf: 120.2 nm

Due to airspace restrictions, no direct flight is permitted between Airport Alpha and Airport Bravo.
Furthermore, for operational reasons, the circuit must incorporate exactly one of two specific route segments: either the connection between Bravo and Charlie, or the connection between Charlie and Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed flight itinerary that visits every airport precisely once before returning to the point of origin, minimizing the total distance flown.
